C1092: ORIGINAL OWNERSHIP ENTRANCE AND ALL SIXTEEN WALL SIGNS
12 October 2026

This file specifies the original all-angle entrance shared by the C1092
wall classes. It supplies all original markers, owners, seed hulls and
auxiliary-label families. The MMMM exclusion starts from this whole
entrance directly. The MMMP and MPPM histories use the further exact
mask closures supplied in the companion file.

All twelve open squares have common side 1<a<=1001/1000, closures in
[0,4]^2, and pairwise disjoint interiors. An owned point is strictly
inside its owner. No square angle or auxiliary owner is presumed beyond
the displayed exhaustive alternatives. C1092 is an original marker case;
its place in the global exhaustive marker classification is inherited.


1. MARKERS, GROUPS AND COMPULSORY SEEDS

The sixteen markers, with zero-based indices, are:

    M_0=(1,457/500)
    M_1=(457/500,1)
    M_2=(3,457/500)
    M_3=(1543/500,1)
    M_4=(3,1543/500)
    M_5=(1543/500,3)
    M_6=(1,1543/500)
    M_7=(457/500,3)
    M_8=(33/20,33/20)
    M_9=(47/20,33/20)
    M_10=(47/20,47/20)
    M_11=(33/20,47/20)
    M_12=(457/500,2)
    M_13=(2,457/500)
    M_14=(1543/500,2)
    M_15=(2,1543/500)

Owner groups and strict seed hulls B_i:
    owner 0; group {0,1}; B_0=Hull((457/500,1),(1,457/500),(1,1))
    owner 1; group {2,3}; B_1=Hull((3,457/500),(1543/500,1),(3,1))
    owner 2; group {4,5}; B_2=Hull((3,3),(1543/500,3),(3,1543/500))
    owner 3; group {6,7}; B_3=Hull((457/500,3),(1,3),(1,1543/500))
    owner 4; group {8}; B_4=Hull((33/20,33/20))
    owner 5; group {9}; B_5=Hull((47/20,33/20))
    owner 6; group {10}; B_6=Hull((47/20,47/20))
    owner 7; group {11}; B_7=Hull((33/20,47/20))
    owner 8; group {12}; B_8=Hull((457/500,2))
    owner 9; group {13}; B_9=Hull((2,457/500))
    owner 10; group {14}; B_10=Hull((1543/500,2))
    owner 11; group {15}; B_11=Hull((2,1543/500))

All sixteen markers are owned, and no marker outside an owner's displayed
group is inside that owner. The four corner-pair seeds use the previously
proved paired-corner inner-point lemma. The remaining seeds are single
markers. Thus every displayed seed hull is strictly inside its owner.


2. FULL AUXILIARY OWNERSHIP FAMILIES

Use the following two ordered ten-point lists, both in lexicographic order:

    F_0=(1,87/50)
    F_1=(1,113/50)
    F_2=(8/5,1)
    F_3=(8/5,3)
    F_4=(2,87/50)
    F_5=(2,113/50)
    F_6=(12/5,1)
    F_7=(12/5,3)
    F_8=(3,87/50)
    F_9=(3,113/50)
    G_0=(1,8/5)
    G_1=(1,12/5)
    G_2=(87/50,1)
    G_3=(87/50,2)
    G_4=(87/50,3)
    G_5=(113/50,1)
    G_6=(113/50,2)
    G_7=(113/50,3)
    G_8=(3,8/5)
    G_9=(3,12/5)

A ten-bit integer f denotes its exact owned subset of F, and g denotes its
exact owned subset of G. The combined label m=f+1024g describes the exact
owned subset of S=(F_0,...,F_9,G_0,...,G_9). Two labels are disjoint if they
share no bit. A point absent from a label is excluded from that owner;
not every auxiliary point is required to be owned by some owner.

For F the six exceptional marker pairs are the four corner pairs and
{8,11},{9,10}; for G they are the corner pairs and {8,9},{10,11}. The
pair-covering theorem says that a square avoiding a covering owns one
of its six pairs. In C1092 the exceptional owners are exactly 0,1,2,3
for both coverings. Thus each of owners 4,...,11 owns between one and
three points of each covering, and each corner owner owns between zero
and two. These bounds come from eight compulsory incidences among ten
available points, leaving only two spare incidences. A candidate subset
must contain every covering point already in its owner's seed hull.

The preliminary geometric subset test is the same explicit four-part
test proved in C974/01_entrance_and_85_vectors.txt, Sections 2 and 3.
For clarity its complete arithmetic data are restated here. Given owned
subset T, put H=Hull(B_i union T); let E be the markers outside the group
and the unowned points of the currently tested covering. Reject T if:

  (a) H contains a point of E;
  (b) vertices A,B of H and P,Q in E have |P-Q|^2<1,
      (P-A).(Q-A)>0, (P-B).(Q-B)>0, and P,A,Q,B is strictly convex
      in cyclic order;
  (c) H contains (1.65,1.65) and one of (1,2.26),(2,2.26), while E
      contains (1,1.74),(1.65,2.35),(2,1.74), or any of their eight
      simultaneous container symmetries has this property;
  (d) H contains (.914,2),(1,1.74),(1.74,2), while E contains
      (1,1.6),(1,2.4),(1.65,1.65), or any of their eight simultaneous
      container symmetries has this property.

The symmetries exchange coordinates and independently reflect across
x=2,y=2. Convex cyclic order uses four nonzero cross products of one sign.
These are the previously proved convexity and four/five/six-point
obstructions. Their strict hypotheses hold for H by construction.

Enumerate every F subset and G subset within the displayed size bounds
that includes the seed's compulsory covering points and passes this test.
Their exact surviving single-cover lists are:

to their union. Repeatedly sweep owners in order 0,...,11; for each owner's

intersection of its labels. Stop when no label changes. The exact final

Define the full family V exactly, without an additional selection:

    V={ (m_0,...,m_11) in M_0 x ... x M_11:
          every two components are disjoint as auxiliary subsets }.

This finite product-and-disjointness formula specifies every candidate;
there is no unspecified survivor list. Exact enumeration gives

    |V|=55126.

The file 07_all_55126_ownership_vectors.txt lists that entire set in
lexicographic integer-tuple order. It was independently reconstructed
from the original predicates, and the all-angle MMMM replay rebuilt it
again before initializing any square domain. The identification digest is
    e0457fec8d64bf3f7280eddd6e6b9c9bac740c98819081d2f57a9bd595875f0c.

3. CLOSED WALL SIGNS AND THEIR EXACT SYMMETRY COVER

A wall sign is a four-tuple in owner order 8,9,10,11. Its corresponding
center coordinates are y,x,y,x. The letter m means coordinate>=2 and
p means coordinate<=2. Both inequalities are closed; every center
therefore satisfies at least one sign, with both allowed at equality.
The sixteen sign tuples cover all actual C1092 configurations.

For any container symmetry T, the marker coordinates give a permutation
of the twelve owner groups and a permutation of the twenty auxiliary
points. Every seed hull maps exactly to its permuted seed hull. All four
subset tests and the size budgets are invariant under these symmetries,
so the complete family V maps to itself. This exact equality was also
checked directly on all 55,126 tuples in the fresh all-angle replay.

For a wall coordinate, write its centered transformed coordinate as
z'-2=epsilon(z-2), epsilon in {-1,1}. Its sign therefore transforms by
s'=epsilon*s at the permuted wall owner. This gives the following four
complete disjoint orbits of the sixteen labels:

    mmmm: mmmm, mpmp, pmpm, pppp
    mmmp: mmmp, mmpm, mpmm, mppp, pmmm, pmpp, ppmp, pppm
    mmpp: mmpp, ppmm
    mppm: mppm, pmmp

The orbit sizes are 4,8,2,2 and sum to sixteen. Transforming all actual
squares, centers and point ownerships by T proves that an exclusion of
one representative excludes its entire orbit. This is an exhaustive
closed cover, including the center-midline boundary cases.

The companion MMMM and MMMP histories eliminate the first two complete
orbits. The separate opposite-pair theorem handles MMPP, and the separate
MPPM application handles the final two-sign orbit. This file supplies
the common original entrance, not a claim that symmetry itself excludes
any orbit.
